title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Teaching and Learning
supports_claim: The U.S. Department of Education reported that AI tutoring systems risk pedagogical narrowing and algorithmic bias against students with disabilities and English learners.
limitations: Government policy report providing recommendations; does not constitute regulatory enforcement or quantitative empirical testing of specific products.

title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
supports_claim: The study found that GPT detectors misclassified 61.3 percent of TOEFL essays written by non-native English speakers as AI-generated while near-zero false positive rate for native speakers.
limitations: Empirical study of 7 detectors on specific essay corpora; results may not generalize to all writing detection products or all student populations.

title: Eating Disorders Chatbot Tessa Taken Down After Dispensing Weight-Loss Advice
supports_claim: KFF Health News reported that the NEDA Tessa chatbot advised users with active eating disorders to maintain a daily calorie deficit and track food intake with restrictive methods.
limitations: Reporting based on user-shared screenshots and expert commentary; no independent technical audit of the chatbot system was published.

title: Character.AI Lawsuit After Florida Teen Suicide
supports_claim: CBS News reported the Garcia v. Character Technologies lawsuit alleging a 14-year-old student developed severe emotional dependence on an AI chatbot without minor safety barriers before his death.
limitations: News reporting on court complaint allegations not adjudicated findings; adolescent suicide involves multifaceted mental health factors beyond AI interaction.

title: Law 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: Vietnam AI Law took effect on 2026-03-01 and establishes a risk-based regulatory framework for AI systems including high-risk classification and conformity assessment requirements.
limitations: Exact obligations depend on implementing instruments and specific use case classification against the high-risk list.

title: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg high-risk AI list
supports_claim: The decision explicitly designates AI systems in education as high-risk including self-learning content systems and automated testing and evaluation systems with transition deadline of 2027-09-01.
limitations: A use case must be matched to the full official list; title metadata alone is insufficient for definitive classification.

title: EU AI Act implementation timeline
supports_claim: The Commission identifies education and vocational training AI as a high-risk area under Annex III point 3 including systems that evaluate learning outcomes and steer learning processes.
limitations: Implementation dates and delegated acts can change; re-check before deployment.
